title: Inside the Mind of a Master Procrastinator | Tim Urban | TED

lines.en: So in college,
I was a government major,
which means I had to write a lot of papers.
Now, when a normal student writes a paper,
lines.ko: 보통의 학생은 과제를 할 때 이런 식으로 일을 분산할 겁니다.

lines.en: they might spread the work out a little like this.
lines.ko: 보통의 학생은 과제를 할 때 이런 식으로 일을 분산할 겁니다.

lines.en: So, you know --
(Laughter)
you get started maybe a little slowly,
but you get enough done in the first week
that, with some heavier days later on,
everything gets done, things stay civil.
(Laughter)
And I would want to do that like that.
That would be the plan.
I would have it all ready to go,
but then, actually, the paper would come along,
and then I would kind of do this.
(Laughter)
And that would happen every single paper.
But then came my 90-page senior thesis,
a paper you're supposed to spend a year on.
And I knew for a paper like that, my normal work flow was not an option.
lines.ko: 이런 과제는 평소에 하던대로 하면 안 된다는 걸 알고 있었어요.

lines.en: It was way too big a project.
So I planned things out,
and I decided I kind of had to go something like this.
This is how the year would go.
So I'd start off light,
and I'd bump it up in the middle months,
and then at the end, I would kick it up into high gear
lines.ko: 마지막에는 기운 좀 내서 하는 거죠.

lines.en: just like a little staircase.
How hard could it be to walk up the stairs?
lines.ko: 계단 좀 오르는 게 얼마나 힘들겠어요?

lines.en: No big deal, right?
But then, the funniest thing happened.
Those first few months?
They came and went,
lines.ko: 그냥 시간이 지나갔고 제가 별로 한 게 없었어요.

lines.en: and I couldn't quite do stuff.
lines.ko: 그냥 시간이 지나갔고 제가 별로 한 게 없었어요.

lines.en: So we had an awesome new revised plan.
(Laughter)
And then --
(Laughter)
But then those middle months actually went by,
and I didn't really write words,
and so we were here.
And then two months turned into one month,
which turned into two weeks.
And one day I woke up
with three days until the deadline,
still not having written a word,
and so I did the only thing I could:
lines.ko: 그래서 제가 할 수 있는 걸 했죠.

lines.en: I wrote 90 pages over 72 hours,
pulling not one but two all-nighters --
lines.ko: 하루도 아니고 이틀 밤을 꼬박 새서요.

lines.en: humans are not supposed to pull two all-nighters --
lines.ko: 인간이면 이틀 밤을 새고 그러면 안 됩니다.

lines.en: sprinted across campus,
dove in slow motion,
and got it in just at the deadline.
I thought that was the end of everything.
But a week later I get a call,
lines.ko: 그런데 일주일 뒤에 학교에서 전화가 왔습니다.

lines.en: and it's the school.
lines.ko: 그런데 일주일 뒤에 학교에서 전화가 왔습니다.

lines.en: And they say, "Is this Tim Urban?"
And I say, "Yeah."
And they say, "We need to talk about your thesis."
And I say, "OK."
And they say,
"It's the best one we've ever seen."
(Laughter)
(Applause)
That did not happen.
(Laughter)
It was a very, very bad thesis.
(Laughter)
I just wanted to enjoy that one moment when all of you thought,
lines.ko: 저는 그냥 여러분이 이렇게 생각하는 잠깐의 순간을 즐기고 싶었어요.

lines.en: "This guy is amazing!"
(Laughter)
No, no, it was very, very bad.
Anyway, today I'm a writer-blogger guy.
I write the blog Wait But Why.
And a couple of years ago, I decided to write about procrastination.
lines.ko: 몇 년 전에, 미루기에 대해 쓰려고 했었습니다.

lines.en: My behavior has always perplexed the non-procrastinators around me,
lines.ko: 제 행동은 주변에 할 일을 미루지 않는 사람들을 늘 당황하게 했습니다.

lines.en: and I wanted to explain to the non-procrastinators of the world
what goes on in the heads of procrastinators,
lines.ko: 할 일을 미루는 사람의 머릿속에서 벌어지는 일과

lines.en: and why we are the way we are.
Now, I had a hypothesis
that the brains of procrastinators were actually different
than the brains of other people.
And to test this, I found an MRI lab
lines.ko: 이것을 검증하기 위해 MRI 연구실을 찾아서

lines.en: that actually let me scan both my brain
and the brain of a proven non-procrastinator,
lines.ko: 검증된 미루지 않는 사람의 뇌도 스캔해서

lines.en: so I could compare them.
I actually brought them here to show you today.
I want you to take a look carefully to see if you can notice a difference.
I know that if you're not a trained brain expert,
lines.ko: 여러분이 훈련받은 뇌 전문가가 아닌 이상

lines.en: it's not that obvious, but just take a look, OK?
lines.ko: 차이가 확연히 보이진 않겠지만 그래도 한 번 봐주세요.

lines.en: So here's the brain of a non-procrastinator.
(Laughter)
Now ...
here's my brain.
(Laughter)
There is a difference.
Both brains have a Rational Decision-Maker in them,
but the procrastinator's brain
also has an Instant Gratification Monkey.
Now, what does this mean for the procrastinator?
lines.ko: 이게 할 일을 미루는 사람에게 무슨 의미일까요?

lines.en: Well, it means everything's fine until this happens.
lines.ko: 이 일이 벌어지기 전까진 모든 게 괜찮다는 뜻입니다.

lines.en: [This is a perfect time to get some work done.] [Nope!]
So the Rational Decision-Maker will make the rational decision
to do something productive,
lines.ko: 생산적인 일을 하기 위해 합리적인 결정을 할 겁니다.

lines.en: but the Monkey doesn't like that plan,
lines.ko: 하지만 원숭이는 그걸 안 좋아하기 때문에

lines.en: so he actually takes the wheel,
and he says, "Actually, let's read the entire Wikipedia page
lines.ko: "낸시 케리건과 토냐 하딩 스캔들의 위키피디아 페이지를 몽땅 읽자구.

lines.en: of the Nancy Kerrigan/ Tonya Harding scandal,
lines.ko: "낸시 케리건과 토냐 하딩 스캔들의 위키피디아 페이지를 몽땅 읽자구.

lines.en: because I just remembered that that happened.
(Laughter)
Then --
(Laughter)
Then we're going to go over to the fridge,
to see if there's anything new in there since 10 minutes ago.
lines.ko: 10분 전보다 뭐 새로운 게 없는지 보자고.

lines.en: After that, we're going to go on a YouTube spiral
that starts with videos of Richard Feynman talking about magnets
lines.ko: 리처드 파인만이 자석을 설명하는 영상으로 시작해서

lines.en: and ends much, much later with us watching interviews
with Justin Bieber's mom.
lines.ko: 저스틴 비버 엄마를 인터뷰하는 영상을 보는 거야.

lines.en: (Laughter)
"All of that's going to take a while,
so we're not going to really have room on the schedule for any work today.
lines.ko: 오늘은 아무 일도 할 시간이 없어. 미안!"

lines.en: Sorry!"
(Sigh)
Now, what is going on here?
The Instant Gratification Monkey does not seem like a guy
lines.ko: 순간적 만족감 원숭이는 운전대를 잡게 하고 싶어할 만한 애가 아닙니다.

lines.en: you want behind the wheel.
lines.ko: 운전대를 잡게 하고 싶어할 만한 애가 아닙니다.

lines.en: He lives entirely in the present moment.
lines.ko: 그는 완전히 현재의 순간 속에서만 살고 있죠.

lines.en: He has no memory of the past, no knowledge of the future,
lines.ko: 과거의 기억이나 미래에 대한 지식이 없고

lines.en: and he only cares about two things:
easy and fun.
Now, in the animal world, that works fine.
If you're a dog
and you spend your whole life doing nothing other than easy and fun things,
lines.ko: 평생을 쉽고 재미있는 것만 하면서 지낸다면

lines.en: you're a huge success!
(Laughter)
And to the Monkey,
humans are just another animal species.
You have to keep well-slept, well-fed and propagating into the next generation,
lines.ko: 잘 자고, 잘 먹고, 잘 번식하기만 하면 되는 겁니다.

lines.en: which in tribal times might have worked OK.
But, if you haven't noticed, now we're not in tribal times.
We're in an advanced civilization, and the Monkey does not know what that is.
lines.ko: 지금은 선진 문명의 시대인데 원숭이는 그게 뭔지 모르죠.

lines.en: Which is why we have another guy in our brain,
lines.ko: 그렇기 때문에 우리 뇌에는 다른 존재가 또 있어요.

lines.en: the Rational Decision-Maker,
who gives us the ability to do things no other animal can do.
lines.ko: 우리에게 동물이 할 수 없는 일을 할 수 있는 능력을 주죠.

lines.en: We can visualize the future.
We can see the big picture.
We can make long-term plans.
And he wants to take all of that into account.
lines.ko: 합리적 의사결정자는 이걸 모두 고려하려고 합니다.

lines.en: And he wants to just have us do
lines.ko: 지금 현재 합리적인 일을 하도록 만들고 싶어 합니다.

lines.en: whatever makes sense to be doing right now.
lines.ko: 지금 현재 합리적인 일을 하도록 만들고 싶어 합니다.

lines.en: Now, sometimes it makes sense
lines.ko: 어떤 때에는 쉽고 재미있는 일을 하는 게

lines.en: to be doing things that are easy and fun,
like when you're having dinner or going to bed
or enjoying well-earned leisure time.
That's why there's an overlap.
Sometimes they agree.
But other times, it makes much more sense
lines.ko: 하지만 떄로는 힘들고 별로 즐겁지 않아도

lines.en: to be doing things that are harder and less pleasant,
lines.ko: 일을 하는 게 훨씬 합리적일 때가 있어요.

lines.en: for the sake of the big picture.
And that's when we have a conflict.
And for the procrastinator,
that conflict tends to end a certain way every time,
lines.ko: 그런 갈등이 늘 같은 방식으로 끝납니다.

lines.en: leaving him spending a lot of time in this orange zone,
lines.ko: 합리적 왕국을 벗어난 쉽고 재미있는 왕국인

lines.en: an easy and fun place that's entirely out of the Makes Sense circle.
lines.ko: 이 주황색 지대에서 많은 시간을 보내게 되죠.

lines.en: I call it the Dark Playground.
(Laughter)
Now, the Dark Playground is a place
that all of you procrastinators out there know very well.
lines.ko: 일을 미루는 사람들이 다 잘 아는 곳이죠.

lines.en: It's where leisure activities happen
at times when leisure activities are not supposed to be happening.
lines.ko: 어떤 때는 여가활동을 하면 안 될 때도 합니다.

lines.en: The fun you have in the Dark Playground
isn't actually fun, because it's completely unearned,
lines.ko: 사실 재미있지는 않아요. 놀 자격이 없으니까요.

lines.en: and the air is filled with guilt, dread, anxiety, self-hatred --
lines.ko: 그 곳의 공기는 죄책감, 공포, 불안, 자기혐호로 가득한데

lines.en: all of those good procrastinator feelings.
lines.ko: 모두 일 미루는 사람들이 느끼는 감정이죠.

lines.en: And the question is, in this situation, with the Monkey behind the wheel,
how does the procrastinator ever get himself over here to this blue zone,
lines.ko: 어떻게 일 미루는 사람들이 파란 지대로 가느냐는 거죠.

lines.en: a less pleasant place, but where really important things happen?
lines.ko: 덜 즐겁지만 중요한 일이 벌어지는 곳에요.

lines.en: Well, turns out the procrastinator has a guardian angel,
lines.ko: 다행히 일을 미루는 사람에게는 수호천사가 있답니다.

lines.en: someone who's always looking down on him and watching over him
lines.ko: 언제나 그를 내려다 보며 가장 암울한 순간에 지켜주는 존재인데

lines.en: in his darkest moments --
someone called the Panic Monster.
(Laughter)
Now, the Panic Monster is dormant most of the time,
but he suddenly wakes up anytime a deadline gets too close
lines.ko: 마감기한이 코 앞으로 다가오거나, 공개적으로 망신당하거나,

lines.en: or there's danger of public embarrassment,
a career disaster or some other scary consequence.
lines.ko: 무시무시한 후환의 위험이 있는 경우에 갑자기 깨어납니다.

lines.en: And importantly, he's the only thing the Monkey is terrified of.
lines.ko: 중요한 것은 그게 원숭이가 무서워하는 유일한 존재라는 거예요.

lines.en: Now, he became very relevant in my life pretty recently,
lines.ko: 최근까지도 제 인생에서 매우 가까운 존재였습니다.

lines.en: because the people of TED reached out to me about six months ago
and invited me to do a TED Talk.
(Laughter)
Now, of course, I said yes.
It's always been a dream of mine to have done a TED Talk in the past.
lines.ko: 항상 TED강연을 하고 싶다는 꿈이 있었거든요.

lines.en: (Laughter)
(Applause)
But in the middle of all this excitement,
the Rational Decision-Maker seemed to have something else on his mind.
lines.ko: 합리적 의사결정자가 다른 생각이 들었나 봅니다.

lines.en: He was saying, "Are we clear on what we just accepted?
Do we get what's going to be now happening one day in the future?
lines.ko: 미래의 어느 날 무슨 일이 일어날건지 확실히 이해하지?

lines.en: We need to sit down and work on this right now."
lines.ko: 지금 당장 앉아서 시작해야 해." 라고 합니다.

lines.en: And the Monkey said, "Totally agree, but let's just open Google Earth
lines.ko: 그러자 원숭이가 "전적으로 동의하지만 지금은 그냥 구글어스를 열고

lines.en: and zoom in to the bottom of India, like 200 feet above the ground,
lines.ko: 인도를 더 잘 알기 위해 인도의 남단을 확대해서

lines.en: and scroll up for two and a half hours til we get to the top of the country,
so we can get a better feel for India."
lines.ko: 두 시간 반 동안 위로 스크롤하자." 라고 합니다.

lines.en: (Laughter)
So that's what we did that day.
(Laughter)
As six months turned into four and then two and then one,
the people of TED decided to release the speakers.
And I opened up the website, and there was my face
lines.ko: 웹사이트를 열어보니 제 얼굴이 저를 똑바로 쳐다보고 있는 거예요.

lines.en: staring right back at me.
lines.ko: 제 얼굴이 저를 똑바로 쳐다보고 있는 거예요.

lines.en: And guess who woke up?
(Laughter)
So the Panic Monster starts losing his mind,
lines.ko: 그래서 패닉 괴물이 정신줄을 놓기 시작합니다.

lines.en: and a few seconds later, the whole system's in mayhem.
lines.ko: 몇 초 뒤에는 모든 시스템이 난리가 났죠.

lines.en: (Laughter)
And the Monkey -- remember, he's terrified of the Panic Monster --
boom, he's up the tree!
And finally,
finally, the Rational Decision-Maker can take the wheel
and I can start working on the talk.
Now, the Panic Monster explains
all kinds of pretty insane procrastinator behavior,
lines.ko: 할 일을 미루는 실성한 사람들의 행동을 설명해 줍니다.

lines.en: like how someone like me could spend two weeks
unable to start the opening sentence of a paper,
lines.ko: 과제의 첫 문장도 못 쓰는 저 같은 사람들이

lines.en: and then miraculously find the unbelievable work ethic
to stay up all night and write eight pages.
And this entire situation, with the three characters --
lines.ko: 이 모든 상황이 세 인물로 설명됩니다.

lines.en: this is the procrastinator's system.
It's not pretty, but in the end, it works.
lines.ko: 별로 좋은 모양은 아니지만 최종적으로 효과는 있습니다.

lines.en: This is what I decided to write about on the blog a couple of years ago.
lines.ko: 그래서 몇 년 전에 이것에 대해 블로그에 썼습니다.

lines.en: When I did, I was amazed by the response.
lines.ko: 글을 썼을 때, 사람들의 반응은 놀라웠습니다.

lines.en: Literally thousands of emails came in,
lines.ko: 말 그대로 수 천 통의 이메일을

lines.en: from all different kinds of people from all over the world,
doing all different kinds of things.
These are people who were nurses, bankers, painters, engineers
and lots and lots of PhD students.
lines.ko: 그리고 엄청나게 많은 박사과정 학생들이 있었죠.

lines.en: (Laughter)
And they were all writing, saying the same thing:
"I have this problem too."
But what struck me was the contrast between the light tone of the post
lines.ko: 하지만 제가 놀란 것은 블로그의 글은 가벼운 어조인데

lines.en: and the heaviness of these emails.
lines.ko: 이메일은 매우 진지한 어조로 대조되는 것이었습니다.

lines.en: These people were writing with intense frustration
lines.ko: 이 사람들은 정말 일을 미루는 것 때문에

lines.en: about what procrastination had done to their lives,
lines.ko: 인생이 어떻게 되었는지를 매우 답답해하며 토로했습니다.

lines.en: about what this Monkey had done to them.
And I thought about this, and I said,
well, if the procrastinator's system works, then what's going on?
lines.ko: 일을 미루는 사람의 시스템이 효과가 있는데 왜 이런 거지?

lines.en: Why are all of these people in such a dark place?
lines.ko: 어째서 이 모든 사람들이 암울한 곳에 있는 걸까?

lines.en: Well, it turns out that there's two kinds of procrastination.
lines.ko: 알고 보니 두 종류의 미루기가 있었습니다.

lines.en: Everything I've talked about today, the examples I've given,
lines.ko: 오늘 말씀드린 예시에는 다 마감기한이 있었습니다.

lines.en: they all have deadlines.
And when there's deadlines,
lines.ko: 그 기한이 있을 때는 미루기의 결과는 단기간으로 제한됩니다.

lines.en: the effects of procrastination are contained to the short term
because the Panic Monster gets involved.
But there's a second kind of procrastination
that happens in situations when there is no deadline.
So if you wanted a career where you're a self-starter --
something in the arts, something entrepreneurial --
there's no deadlines on those things at first, because nothing's happening,
not until you've gone out and done the hard work
lines.ko: 나서서 일을 하기 전까지는 아무 일도 일어나지 않으니까요.

lines.en: to get momentum, get things going.
lines.ko: 나서서 일을 하기 전까지는 아무 일도 일어나지 않으니까요.

lines.en: There's also all kinds of important things outside of your career
lines.ko: 직업 이외에 어떤 기한도 없는 중요한 일들은 많이 있습니다.

lines.en: that don't involve any deadlines,
lines.ko: 직업 이외에 어떤 기한도 없는 중요한 일들은 많이 있습니다. 가족을 만나거나 운동하고, 건강을 돌보고,

lines.en: like seeing your family or exercising and taking care of your health,
working on your relationship
or getting out of a relationship that isn't working.
lines.ko: 잘 되지 않는 관계는 정리하는 것 등이죠.

lines.en: Now if the procrastinator's only mechanism of doing these hard things
lines.ko: 일을 미루는 사람이 이런 어려운 일들을 하게 만들 수 있는 유일한 기제가

lines.en: is the Panic Monster, that's a problem,
because in all of these non-deadline situations,
lines.ko: 왜냐하면 이런 모든 일에는 마감기한이 없어서

lines.en: the Panic Monster doesn't show up.
He has nothing to wake up for,
so the effects of procrastination, they're not contained;
lines.ko: 그래서 미루기로 초래되는 결과가 제한되지 않고

lines.en: they just extend outward forever.
And it's this long-term kind of procrastination
that's much less visible and much less talked about
lines.ko: 우습고, 단기적이며, 기한이 있는 종류보다 훨씬 잘 안 보이고 논의가 되지 않습니다.

lines.en: than the funnier, short-term deadline-based kind.
lines.ko: 우습고, 단기적이며, 기한이 있는 종류보다 훨씬 잘 안 보이고 논의가 되지 않습니다.

lines.en: It's usually suffered quietly and privately.
And it can be the source
lines.ko: 이건 상당한 장기적인 불행과 후회의 원천이 될 수 있습니다.

lines.en: of a huge amount of long-term unhappiness, and regrets.
lines.ko: 이건 상당한 장기적인 불행과 후회의 원천이 될 수 있습니다.

lines.en: And I thought, that's why those people are emailing,
lines.ko: 저는 그래서 사람들이 이메일을 보냈다고 봅니다.

lines.en: and that's why they're in such a bad place.
lines.ko: 이래서 그들이 매우 안 좋은 상황에 있는 거죠.

lines.en: It's not that they're cramming for some project.
lines.ko: 그들이 과제를 벼락치기 해서 그런 게 아닙니다.

lines.en: It's that long-term procrastination has made them feel like a spectator,
at times, in their own lives.
lines.ko: 때때로 자신의 삶의 구경꾼같이 느끼게 해서 그런 겁니다.

lines.en: The frustration is not that they couldn't achieve their dreams;
it's that they weren't even able to start chasing them.
lines.ko: 아예 꿈을 향해 출발할 수도 없었기 때문이죠.

lines.en: So I read these emails and I had a little bit of an epiphany --
lines.ko: 그래서 이 메일들을 읽고 약간의 깨달음을 얻었는데

lines.en: that I don't think non-procrastinators exist.
lines.ko: 미루지 않는 사람이란 존재하지 않는다고 봅니다.

lines.en: That's right -- I think all of you are procrastinators.
Now, you might not all be a mess,
lines.ko: 뭐, 여러분은 저희처럼 그렇게 엉망은 아닐지 모르죠.

lines.en: like some of us,
lines.ko: 뭐, 여러분은 저희처럼 그렇게 엉망은 아닐지 모르죠.

lines.en: (Laughter)
and some of you may have a healthy relationship with deadlines,
lines.ko: 여러분은 마감기한이 있는 건전한 사귐이 있을지도 모르지만

lines.en: but remember: the Monkey's sneakiest trick
is when the deadlines aren't there.
Now, I want to show you one last thing.
I call this a Life Calendar.
That's one box for every week of a 90-year life.
lines.ko: 90년의 인생에 한 주마다 상자가 하나씩 있습니다.

lines.en: That's not that many boxes,
especially since we've already used a bunch of those.
lines.ko: 특히 우리는 상자를 이미 많이 썼으니까요.

lines.en: So I think we need to all take a long, hard look at that calendar.
lines.ko: 이 달력을 오랫동안 유심히 볼 필요가 있다고 생각합니다.

lines.en: We need to think about what we're really procrastinating on,
lines.ko: 우리가 정작 무엇을 미루고 있는지 생각해 보아야 합니다.

lines.en: because everyone is procrastinating on something in life.
We need to stay aware of the Instant Gratification Monkey.
lines.ko: 순간적 만족감 원숭이를 늘 의식해야 합니다.

lines.en: That's a job for all of us.
lines.ko: 그게 우리 모두가 해야 할 일이죠.

lines.en: And because there's not that many boxes on there,
it's a job that should probably start today.
Well, maybe not today, but ...
(Laughter)
You know.
Sometime soon.
Thank you.
(Applause)
